newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain sees small rise in government financial cost.
newsitem.headline: Spain sees small rise in government financial cost.

text.p: Spanish Treasury Director General Jaime Caruana said on Tuesday that the recent rise in bond yields would produce only a minimum increase in government financial costs, local news agencies reported.
At the Treasury's monthly auction on Tuesday, three- and 10-year bond yields rose to 5.922 percent from 5.660 percent and to 6.929 percent from 6.898 percent, respectively.
Caruana, speaking at an economic seminar in Madrid, said a possible rise in yields had already been taken into account when the Treasury set its issuance calendar.

The current account of the Spanish Treasury with the Bank of Spain, standing at 2.528 trillion pesetas in December 1996 from 1.561 trillion one year before, had fallen at the beginning of 1997, Caruana added.
The Spanish Treasury used this money during the last two months to compensate for a negative financial inflow, due to the fact it sold less bonds than the amount it paid out in maturing assets.
